subject: tests/test_secret_path_guard.py K4GuardTests.test_k4_timing: the in-process timed guard.check(text) calls of the helper growth rounds (measure_round) and of the nesting probe
change: Each of those calls runs with gc.disable() and restores the prior gc.isenabled() state in finally, as timeit.Timer.timeit does by default. Nothing else in the test changes.

unchanged.criterion: sizes 25k, 50k and 100k; at most 3 rounds; test exponent below 1.5 over per-size raw minima; 5 ms allowance never scaled; absolute bound 0.5 s times the host factor min(4.0, max(1.0, min(reference samples) / 0.188))
unchanged.named_rows: still timed in fresh child processes, with the collector on

upstream_sources.content: Timer.timeit saves gc.isenabled(), calls gc.disable(), runs the timed loop and calls gc.enable() in finally only if the collector was enabled

timeit turns off garbage collection during the timing by default, which makes independent timings more comparable; the disadvantage is that GC may be an important component of the measured function's performance

objects promoted into the oldest generation add to long_lived_pending (1248); a full collection runs only when long_lived_pending reaches a quarter of long_lived_total (1455, 1479); its cost is proportional to the total number of long-lived objects (1460-1461)

upstream_copy_check: the sha256 of each reviewed local copy equals the file served by raw.githubusercontent.com at the pin

python.ci: ubuntu-24.04 runner python3, no setup-python step in the validate job; the failing step's log does not print the version

evidence_classes.covers: local_reproduction: the real test_k4_timing, after discovery imported every test module, as python3 -m unittest does, on this host
the simulated heaps (refs, prefill) and the quadratic k4_shell_words mutant, constructed by the session-0c diagnosis on 2026-10-03

exponent_definitions.test_exponent: the test's criterion, ln((t100k + 0.005) / (t25k + 0.005)) / ln(4) over per-size raw helper minima; a value of 1.5 or more fails
exponent_definitions.raw_pair_exponent: ln(t2n / tn) / ln(2) for direct helper calls at doubling sizes, without the allowance; 1 is linear

ci_signature: In every failing round the helper time doubles from 25k to 50k (minima ratio 1.97 to 1.98), then jumps 5.93 to 8.06 times from 50k to 100k: an excess of 69.63 to 76.29 ms at 100k over twice the 50k minimum, repeated round after round, not growth.

heap_simulation.refs_N: one live list holding N untracked ints, [list(range(10**6, 10**6 + N))]: each full collection traverses it, so the pause grows without changing the tracked-object count
heap_simulation.prefill_K: [[i] for i in range(K)] then gc.collect(1) before the test: shifts when the quarter-of-long-lived trigger fires

final_test_rerun.command: nice -n 19 /usr/bin/python3 -B, the real test after discovery, in the heaps that failed the unchanged test

paired_exponent_capture.method: the same run with the test module's k4_timing_passes wrapped to record the arguments of the final per-helper call made by test_k4_timing (outside every timed window); the unchanged and the final test alternate in each heap

collector_can_also_mask_growth.note: with the collector on, a pause that lands in the 25k window lowers the exponent instead of raising it

quadratic_control_final_test.mutant: k4_shell_words wrapped to run text[i:].count("'") for i in range(0, len(text), 10) before the original: O(n^2 / 10) work
quadratic_control_final_test.other_helpers_note: the mutation is the only difference from the passing runs, so check() also reaches the mutated k4_shell_words on those helpers' texts; their test exponents stay under 1.5 and their helper minima under 0.5 s, so their whole-check minima are what cross the 0.5 s absolute bound

gc_callback_attribution.method: a replay of measure_round with the test module's own k4_run_timing_rounds and k4_timing_passes after discovery, with gc.callbacks recording each collection's generation and duration inside every timed helper window; gc on, then gc off as in the fix, in the same simulated heap
gc_callback_attribution.rows_note: each collector-on failure followed by its collector-off twin (same heap, same helper)

linearity_collector_off.method: direct helper calls (outside check()) at 25k, 50k, 100k, 200k and 400k, minimum of 5 repeats

rejected_alternatives.reason: the pause belongs to whichever window the collector's phase selects: with the collector on, direct calls met generation-2 collections at every size from 25k to 400k (collector_on_direct_calls), so larger sizes move the failure and lengthen every helper's rounds

the recorded CI minima need an allowance of at least 6.6 ms to pass; at that allowance the quadratic controls of test_k4_growth_criterion_controls (16 times the 25k time at 100k) score 1.412 from 4.5 ms and 1.663 from 10 ms, so the 4.5 ms control passes and that test breaks
rejected_alternatives.computed_from: ci_failures helper minima (arithmetic, not a new run)

rejected_alternatives.reason: a full collection per size per round outside the window, 201 to 603 of them for 67 helpers, each costing about the 72.1 to 110.4 ms pause measured in the simulated heaps; the collector also stays on inside the window; not measured

changes process-wide collector state for the rest of the suite (it resets the generation counts and hides the frozen heap from every collection until gc.unfreeze()); Doc/library/gc.rst documents it for fork() memory sharing, and timeit's practice for timing is gc.disable(); a choice of practice, not a failed experiment: with the heap frozen after setup the diagnosis measured raw pair exponents 0.978 to 1.051

limitations: CI's own heap was not instrumented: the CI attribution rests on the matching signature (an excess of 69.63 to 76.29 ms at 100k in every round) and on the local gc-callback attribution in simulated heaps.

With the collector off, cyclic-garbage collection cost is excluded from the measured helper time, the disadvantage Doc/library/timeit.rst L136-141 names; the guard's reference cycles are still collected once the collector is re-enabled.
The simulated heaps and the mutant are synthetic fixtures; they reproduce the failure mode, not CI's exact heap.
